title: Annotatio I §.I Calixtus: Eucharist deformed by papal abuses — reformers right, but weak foresight at the start
pass_a_gloss: The occasion of the Prior Priority B. Georg. Calixtus not tastelessly annotates in these words: The Sacrament of the Eucharist had hitherto been deformed among the Pontificians by many and foul abuses and superstitions, and scarcely any other head of religion had experienced equal calamity: they adored the blessed bread — the abuse removed — because they believed it to be nothing but the very Body itself, and commonly set it forth to be adored; nay they also held and offered a propitiatory sacrifice (the word taken strictly and in its formal signification). And so they most frequently celebrated solitary Masses, as they call them, devoid of Communicants, and rarely with Communicants admitted. The first leaders and Authors of the Reformation were intent on abolishing these errors and pravities, which was altogether right; but such is the weakness of human ingenuity that not all foresaw in those beginnings how that would rightly be done — Judgment on theological controversies §.47, Dutch ed. p. 69 at the end & 70.
pass_b_english: Calixtus notes the occasion of that first priority without tastelessness: among the Pontificians the Eucharist had been deformed by foul abuses and superstitions — scarcely any other head of religion had suffered equal calamity.
They adored the blessed bread as the very Body, set it out for adoration, and offered a propitiatory sacrifice; solitary Masses without communicants were frequent.
The first Reformation leaders rightly meant to abolish those errors — yet human ingenuity is weak, and not all foresaw at the start how it would be done rightly (Judic. §.47, Dutch ed. pp. 69–70).
source_text: Prioris Prioritatis occasionem non insulsè annotat B. Georg. Calixtus hisce verbis: Sacramentum Eucharistiae multis & tetris abusibus & superstitionibus hactenus apud Pontificios deformatum erat & vix aliud religionis caput parem calamitatem expertum: Panem benedictum abusu remoto, quod nihil nisi ipsumissimum corpus crederent esse, adorabant & vulgò adorandum proponebant, quin & sacrificium propitiatorium (vocabulo hôc strictè & in formali significatione accepto) habebant & offerebant. Atque adeo Missas ut vocant solitarias, Communicantium expertes, frequentissimè celebrabant, rarò autem adhibitis Communicantibus. Hisce erroribus & pravitatibus abolendis intenti erant primi Reformationis duces & Autores, quod omnino rectè erat; quae est autem humani ingenii imbecillitas, quomodo id rectè fieret, non omnes in istis initiis providebant, Judic. de controversiis theologicis §.47. Batav. ed. p. 69. in fine & 70.
notes: Calixtus; papal Eucharist abuses; Reformation beginnings.
